theme: Clients keep coming back — repeat business as social proof

linkedin.text:
In B2B event production, repeat business is the most honest performance metric there is.

A client can attend one event and call it a success. But when that same client comes back — and brings a bigger group, a bigger brief, or a new business unit — that's a different signal entirely.

Over 16 years and 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations, the pattern is consistent: the teams that experience a well-executed event don't ask "did we need this?" They ask "how do we do this again?"

For HR and marketing leaders evaluating event partners, that question is worth asking upfront: what percentage of your client base runs a second event with you?

We'll answer that honestly. DM me if you want to talk through what repeat engagement actually looks like in practice.

16 years. 1,500+ events. 130+ destinations. The numbers grow because the people in the room remember how it felt.

If you're building an event experience your team will still talk about next quarter, we'd love to hear what you're working on. DM us. 👇

facebook.text:
The real measure of an event company isn't the first event. It's the second. And the third.

Over 16 years, the majority of our growth has come from clients who came back — not because we asked them to, but because their teams did.

When participants start asking their HR manager "when's the next one?", that's the moment the event stops being a cost line and becomes a retention tool.

1,500+ events. 130+ destinations. A lot of repeat names on the client list.

If you're planning something for your team and want to know what keeps people coming back, drop a comment or send us a DM — happy to share what we've learned.
